operations.specification: Implementation: Generate a new JWT access token and refresh token pair for an unauthenticated visitor. Create a guest session record in the database with the refresh token hash, expiration timestamps, and client metadata. Return both tokens in the response. No input credentials required since this creates a temporary anonymous session. The access token should have a short expiration (e.g., 15 minutes) and the refresh token longer (e.g., 7 days) to allow session persistence.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session for unauthenticated visitors.

This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to obtain a temporary JWT session before accessing registration or login endpoints. The platform requires authentication for all features, so guests must first establish a session token to proceed with account creation.

The operation generates fresh access and refresh tokens, stores the session record in the database with expiration timestamps, and returns the tokens to the client. The returned access token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent API calls.

This is typically the first API call made by a visitor to the platform. Once a guest has tokens, they can use them to access the customer or seller registration endpoints.

requestBody.description: Optional metadata for the guest session creation. No credentials are required for guest sessions.

responseBody.description: The guest session tokens containing access token and refresh token for subsequent authenticated requests.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation: Validate the provided refresh token against the guest_sessions table. Check that the token is not expired and matches a valid session record. Generate a new access token and optionally rotate the refresh token for security. Update the session record with new token hashes and expiration timestamps. Return the new token pair. If the refresh token is invalid or expired, return a 401 error requiring the client to call join again.
operations.description:
Refreshes an existing guest session with new access and refresh tokens.

This endpoint allows guest clients to extend their session validity when the access token expires. The client must provide a valid refresh token obtained from the initial join response or previous refresh response.

The operation validates the refresh token against the stored session record, generates new token pairs, updates the session record with new expiration timestamps, and returns fresh tokens. Token rotation may be implemented for enhanced security.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or revoked, the operation returns a 401 error and the client must call join again to establish a new guest session.

requestBody.description: The refresh token from the existing guest session to exchange for new tokens.

responseBody.description: The new guest session tokens containing fresh access token and refresh token for continued authenticated access.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implementation notes: Validate email uniqueness against ecommerce_mall_customers table. Hash password using bcrypt/argon2. Create customer record with email and password_hash. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with ip, href, referrer, and expiration timestamp. Return tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Register a new customer account with email and password.

Creates a new customer record in the ecommerce_mall_customers table with the provided email address and hashed password. Validates that the email address is unique across all customer accounts. Upon successful registration, establishes a new authenticated session and returns JWT access and refresh tokens.

The session is recorded in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions with connection context including IP address, referring page, and timestamps for security auditing. Customers can immediately use their credentials to access protected endpoints after registration.

This endpoint establishes the customer's identity in the system and issues authentication credentials for subsequent API access.

requestBody.description: Customer registration credentials containing email address and password for the new account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens including access token and refresh token for the newly registered customer session.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implementation notes: Look up customer by email in ecommerce_mall_customers table. Verify password_hash matches provided password using secure comparison. Check account is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Reject if credentials invalid. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions tracking connection context. Return tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing customer with email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email address and password against the ecommerce_mall_customers table. Uses secure password hashing comparison to verify credentials. Rejects authentication if the email is not found, password does not match, or the account has been soft deleted.

Upon successful authentication, generates new JWT access and refresh tokens and creates a session record in ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions capturing the connection context (IP address, referring URL, timestamps) for security monitoring.

The returned access token must be included in subsequent API requests via the Authorization header. The refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

requestBody.description: Customer login credentials containing email address and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens including access token and refresh token for the authenticated customer session.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Implementation notes: Validate the provided refresh token against ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions. Check token is not expired. Look up associated customer from ecommerce_mall_customers table. Verify customer account is active (not deleted). Generate new JWT access token with fresh expiration. Optionally rotate refresh token for security. Return new tokens in IEcommerceMallCustomer.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Refresh an expired or soon-to-expire access token using a valid refresh token.

Accepts a refresh token previously issued during login or registration and returns a new access token without requiring the customer to re-enter credentials. Validates the refresh token against the session records and verifies the associated customer account remains active.

For enhanced security, this operation may also issue a new refresh token (token rotation) and invalidate the previous one to prevent replay attacks. The refresh token itself is stored in the ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table with expiration tracking.

Use this endpoint when the access token expires (typically returns 401 Unauthorized) to maintain the customer's session without interrupting their workflow.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token obtained from previous login or registration.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens including fresh access token and potentially new refresh token for continued session.

operations.specification: Implement seller registration (join) operation. Verify email uniqueness against ecommerce_mall_sellers table. Hash password using bcrypt. Create seller record with approval_status='pending'. Create initial seller registration record in ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations with status='pending'. Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. Create session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions capturing IP, href, referrer from request headers. Return tokens and seller info. Error scenarios: duplicate email (409), invalid email format (400), password too weak (400).
operations.description:
Register a new seller account on the platform. Sellers must provide a unique email address and password to create an account. Upon successful registration, the seller account is created with pending approval status and requires administrator review before products can be listed. The operation creates a seller registration application that tracks the approval workflow.

The registration process validates email uniqueness, enforces password strength requirements, and securely hashes the password using bcrypt. A JWT access token and refresh token are issued upon successful registration, allowing immediate authentication while awaiting approval.

Seller accounts with pending status can log in but cannot create products or list items for sale until an administrator approves the registration.

requestBody.description: Seller registration credentials containing email and password for account creation

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller session with JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account details including approval status

operations.name: join

Create session record in ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer). Return tokens and seller info including approval_status. Error scenarios: invalid credentials (401), account not found (401), account deleted (401).
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing seller using email and password credentials. This operation validates the provided credentials against the stored password hash and establishes a new JWT authentication session.

Upon successful authentication, the system issues fresh access and refresh tokens and records the session with connection metadata (IP address, origin URL, referrer) for security auditing. The response includes the seller's current approval status, which determines whether they can list products or must wait for administrator approval.

Soft-deleted accounts cannot log in. The operation supports the complete authentication flow for approved, pending, and rejected sellers to check their account status.

requestBody.description: Seller login credentials containing email and password for authentication

responseBody.description: Authenticated seller session with JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account details including approval status

Verify session belongs to the authenticated seller and has not expired. Generate new JWT access token with updated expiration. Optionally rotate refresh token for security. Update session record with new token information and extended expiration. Return new tokens and seller info. Error scenarios: invalid refresh token (401), expired session (401), seller not found (401).
operations.description:
Renew an expired or nearly-expired JWT access token using a valid refresh token. This operation extends the seller's authenticated session without requiring re-entry of credentials.

The refresh token is validated against the active sessions stored in the ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions table. Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued with a fresh expiration timestamp. The session record is updated to reflect the continued activity.

This operation is essential for maintaining long-lived sessions while adhering to JWT security best practices through short-lived access tokens and periodic refresh.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token to exchange for new access credentials

responseBody.description: Refreshed seller session with new JWT access token, refresh token, and seller account details

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Join operation for administrator accounts. This is typically used when a user (customer or seller) has been approved as an administrator through the AdminPromotionRequest flow. The operation validates the email and password match an existing admin record with 'active' status. Upon successful validation, creates a new session in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT access token and refresh token. Capture client metadata (ip, href, referrer) for security auditing. Hash the provided password using BCrypt and compare against password_hash. Set token expiration based on configuration (e.g., access token 15 minutes, refresh token 30 days). Return both tokens in IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized response.
operations.description:
Administrator join operation. Administrators are created through the promotion request flow (AdminPromotionRequest) approved by super administrators, not through public registration. This operation authenticates an existing admin account using email and password credentials.

Validates the email exists in ecommerce_mall_admins, verifies the BCrypt password_hash matches the provided password, and confirms the account status is 'active' (suspended or banned accounts cannot authenticate). Administrators have two privilege grades: 'regular' (standard admin permissions) and 'super_admin' (can promote/demote other admins).

Upon successful authentication, creates a new session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT tokens (access and refresh), captures connection metadata (IP address, page URL, referrer) for security audit trails, and returns the authorization tokens with admin profile information.

requestBody.description: Administrator join credentials including email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authorization response containing JWT access token, refresh token, administrator profile (id, email, grade, status, nickname), and token expiration information.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Login operation for administrators. Validates email and password against ecommerce_mall_admins table. Check that status is 'active' (reject suspended or banned accounts). Verify BCrypt password_hash. On success, create a session in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT tokens including: access token (short-lived, e.g., 15 min) and refresh token (long-lived, e.g., 30 days). Capture IP, href, referrer from request headers for security audit. Set expired_at based on refresh token lifetime. Return IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized containing tokens and admin profile (id, email, grade, status, nickname).
operations.description:
Administrator login operation. Authenticates administrators using email and password credentials stored in the ecommerce_mall_admins table.

The operation performs multiple validations: verifies the email exists, checks the account status is 'active' (suspended or banned administrators cannot log in), and validates the password against the BCrypt password_hash. Administrators have two grades: 'regular' (standard admin with seller approval, category management, and oversight permissions) and 'super_admin' (additional privileges to promote/demote administrators and approve admin promotion requests).

Upon successful authentication, creates a session record in ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions with JWT access and refresh tokens. Captures security metadata including IP address, referring URL (href), and HTTP referrer for audit trail purposes. Returns the authorization tokens along with the administrator's profile information.

requestBody.description: Administrator login credentials with email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorization response with JWT access token, refresh token, and administrator profile including id, email, grade (regular/super_admin), status, and nickname.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refresh operation for administrator sessions. Accepts a refresh token in the request body and validates it against the ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions table. Look up the session by matching the token and ensure it has not expired (expired_at > now()). On valid token, issue a new access token with updated expiration time. The refresh token itself may be rotated (optional security practice) or kept the same. Update the session record if token rotation is implemented. Return IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized with the new access token. If the session has expired or the token is invalid, return 401 Unauthorized.
operations.description:
Token refresh operation for administrator authentication. Allows administrators to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials by presenting a valid refresh token.

The operation validates the provided refresh token against the ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions table, checking that the session exists and has not expired (expired_at timestamp is in the future). The refresh token is linked to the administrator via the admin_id foreign key relationship.

Upon successful validation, generates a new JWT access token with fresh expiration time. Implementing token rotation (issuing a new refresh token and invalidating the old one) is recommended for enhanced security but optional. Returns IEcommerceMallAdmin.IAuthorized containing the new access token, the refresh token (new or existing), and the administrator's profile information.

If the session has expired or the token is invalid/not found, returns 401 Unauthorized error requiring the administrator to log in again.

requestBody.description: Refresh token request containing the refresh token to exchange for a new access token.

responseBody.description: Authorization response with new JWT access token, the refresh token (rotated or original), and administrator profile information.

operations.specification: Super administrator registration operation. Creates a new super admin account with email and password. Implementation steps: 1) Validate request body contains email and password meeting business rules (email format, password complexity). 2) Check email uniqueness against ecommerce_mall_super_admins table - reject if exists. 3) Hash password using secure algorithm (bcrypt/Argon2). 4) Generate UUID for new record. 5) Insert into ecommerce_mall_super_admins with grade='super_admin', created_at/updated_at current timestamp. 6) Generate JWT access and refresh tokens. 7) Create session record in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions with token metadata (IP, href, referrer from request context, created_at, expired_at). 8) Return IEcommerceMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized containing tokens and super admin identity.
operations.description:
Register a new super administrator account.

Creates a new super administrator account with email-based authentication. The super administrator represents the highest privilege level in the platform hierarchy with abilities to approve admin promotion requests, promote/demote administrators, and manage the admin hierarchy.

Email must be unique across all super admin accounts. Password is securely hashed before storage. Upon successful registration, a JWT session is established with both access and refresh tokens returned. The session metadata including IP address and request context is recorded for audit purposes.

This operation is available publicly for initial super admin creation and requires no authentication.

requestBody.description: Super administrator registration credentials containing email and password for new account creation.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and super administrator identity returned upon successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.description:
Authenticate a super administrator with email and password credentials.

Validates the provided email and password against the stored credentials in the ecommerce_mall_super_admins table. Only active accounts (not soft deleted) can authenticate. The email field is unique per account and serves as the login identifier.

Upon successful credential validation, a new JWT session is established. Both access and refresh tokens are generated and returned. The session is recorded in the ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions table with metadata including client IP address, page URL, and referrer for security monitoring. Previous sessions remain valid until they expire.

This operation is publicly accessible and requires no prior authentication.

requestBody.description: Super administrator login credentials containing email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and super administrator identity returned upon successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Super administrator token refresh operation. Issues new access token using valid refresh token. Implementation steps: 1) Extract and validate the refresh token from the IEcommerceMallSuperAdmin.IRefresh request body. 2) Verify token signature and expiration. 3) Look up associated session in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions to ensure session is still valid/active. 4) Query super admin account from ecommerce_mall_super_admins to verify account still exists and is not deleted. 5) Generate new access token (and optionally new refresh token based on security policy). 6) Update session expiration if using sliding expiration. 7) Return IEcommerceMallSuperAdmin.IAuthorized with new tokens.
operations.description:
Refresh the access token for an authenticated super administrator session.

Accepts a valid refresh token and issues a new access token, allowing the super administrator to maintain their session without re-authenticating with credentials. The refresh token is validated for authenticity and expiration.

The operation verifies the associated session exists in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions and that the super administrator account remains active (not soft deleted). This enables continuous access management while maintaining security through token rotation.

This operation is publicly accessible and requires no prior authentication header - the refresh token itself serves as the authentication credential in the request body.

requestBody.description: Token refresh request containing the refresh token used to obtain a new access token.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens returned upon successful token refresh.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of all customer accounts for administrative oversight.

This operation provides administrators with comprehensive search capabilities to browse the complete customer base. It supports filtering by partial email matching, account status (active or banned), and registration date ranges. The response includes customer summary information optimized for list displays, showing essential identification and status information without exposing sensitive details.

Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and support cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large customer databases. Sorting options include newest first, email alphabetical order, and account status grouping.

Query the ecommerce_mall_customers table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters:
- email: Partial string match (LIKE query with wildcards)
- accountStatus: Exact match filtering for 'active' or 'banned' status
- registrationDateRange: Date range filter on created_at field
- displayName: Partial match on related CustomerProfile.display_name

Validate that the requesting actor has admin role before executing query.

Use cursor-based pagination (limit/after) for efficient large dataset navigation.

Join with ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles to include display name in results.
Exclude soft-deleted accounts from results unless explicitly requested.

Return IPageIEcommerceMallCustomer.ISummary with:

- profile display name

Retrieve detailed information about a specific customer account.

This operation returns the complete customer record identified by the provided customerId UUID. The response includes the customer's email address, account creation timestamp, and last update timestamp.

For security reasons, sensitive fields such as password hash are not included in the response. The deleted_at field indicates whether the customer account has been soft-deleted.

This endpoint is typically used by customers viewing their own account details or by administrators performing account oversight. Access control ensures customers can only view their own data unless they have administrative privileges.

Query the ecommerce_mall_customers table by primary key id matching the customerId path parameter.

Return fields: id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Error handling:
- Return 404 Not Found if no customer exists with the given customerId
- Return 403 Forbidden if the requesting customer attempts to access another customer's data without admin privileges

Update the authenticated customer's profile information.

This operation allows customers to modify their public-facing profile data including display name and phone number. Both fields are editable throughout the account lifetime and changes take effect immediately upon saving.

The system verifies that the authenticated customer is modifying their own profile. Profile edits do not create snapshots as profile information is not subject to the snapshot principle that applies to transactional data.

If the submitted data fails validation (e.g., invalid phone number format), the request is rejected with specific validation error details.

operations.specification: Validate the authenticated customer's identity from the session. Verify the customer has a profile (created automatically during registration). Validate the request body fields: display name (string, optional for update), phone number (string, must be valid format). Update the profile record in ecommerce_mall_customers table. Return the updated profile with current values. Handle validation errors by returning 400 with specific field errors. Handle authentication errors by returning 401 if no valid session exists.

Sessions include connection metadata such as IP address, referrer URL, and creation timestamp. Expired sessions are retained for security auditing purposes. Results are paginated with cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large session histories.

Requires authentication. Customers can only access their own sessions. Administrators may have broader access depending on implementation policies.

operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table with pagination and filtering.

Authorization: Verify authenticated customer can only access sessions where ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches their own customer ID. Administrators may bypass this restriction based on role.

Filtering support:
- created_at date range (from/to)
- expired_at date range for expired sessions
- expiration status filter (active only, expired only, or all)
- ip address partial matching for security analysis

Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination with created_at as the cursor field for consistent ordering. Support configurable page sizes (default 20, max 100).

Sorting: Primary sort by created_at DESC (newest first), secondary sort by id for stability.

Response fields include: id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at, and a flag indicating if the session is currently active (expired_at > now).

operations.description:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific customer session by its unique identifier.

This operation allows authenticated customers to view their own session details for security auditing and account management purposes. The session information includes connection metadata such as IP address, page URL where the session was initiated, and HTTP referrer header value. Temporal fields indicate when the session was created and when it expires.

Session data is sensitive and access is strictly limited to the customer who owns the session. The system validates ownership before returning any session information. If the requested session does not belong to the authenticated customer, the system returns a not-found response to prevent session ID enumeration attacks.

Active sessions can be monitored by customers to detect unauthorized access or unusual login patterns from unexpected IP addresses or referrers.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions table by primary key id matching the provided sessionId path parameter.

Validate that the session's ecommerce_mall_customer_id matches the authenticated customer's ID. If ownership verification fails, return 404 Not Found (do not reveal the session belongs to another user).

Return the complete session record including: id, ecommerce_mall_customer_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at.

Edge case handling:
- If sessionId is not a valid UUID format, return 400 Bad Request
- If session does not exist, return 404 Not Found
- If session exists but belongs to different customer, return 404 Not Found (security through obscurity)
- If session has expired, still return it if owned by requesting customer (customer can see their expired sessions)

4. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
5. Check session expiration: compare expired_at against current timestamp
6. Return full session data including: id, guest_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at
7. Include the related guest entity in the response if the DTO structure supports nested relations

Edge cases:
- Expired sessions should still be returned (not filtered) as this is a retrieval operation for audit/debugging
- Session expiration status can be derived from comparing expired_at to current time
- The referrer and href fields capture the visitor's navigation context at session creation

The ownership verification is performed before any update is applied. If the address does not belong to the requesting customer, the system will respond as if the address does not exist (to prevent address ID enumeration attacks). The system logs any unauthorized access attempts for security monitoring purposes.

After a successful update, the address will reflect the new information in the customer's address book for future order shipments. This update does NOT affect addresses already associated with placed orders, which maintain their original information for record-keeping purposes.

6. Validate all required fields are present in the request body: recipientName, phoneNumber, streetAddress, city, stateOrProvince, postalCode, country

operations.description:
Permanently delete a customer's shipping address.

This operation removes the specified address from the customer's address book. The address will no longer be available for selection during checkout.

**Ownership Verification**: The system verifies that the address belongs to the authenticated customer. If the address does not belong to the customer, the request is rejected with a response identical to a non-existent address to prevent address enumeration attacks.

**Default Address Handling**: If the deleted address was designated as the default shipping address, the customer must select a different address to become the new default before the deletion can proceed. This ensures the customer always has a default address for checkout convenience.

**Order History Preservation**: Deleting an address does not affect any existing orders. Orders preserve a complete snapshot of the address at the time of purchase for record-keeping and legal purposes. Historical orders will continue to display the address information as it existed when the order was placed.

**Authorization**: Only the customer who owns the address can delete it. Sellers and administrators cannot delete customer addresses.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement the following business logic:

1. **Authentication Check**: Verify the customer is authenticated.

2. **Ownership Verification**: Query the address record and verify that address.customerId matches the authenticated customer's ID.
   - If no address exists with the given addressId OR the address belongs to a different customer: Return 404 Not Found (do not reveal whether the address exists to prevent enumeration attacks).
   - Log the unauthorized access attempt for security review.

3. **Default Address Check**: Check if the address is designated as the customer's default shipping address.
   - If it is the default address:
     - Option A: Automatically clear the default designation and proceed with deletion.
     - Option B: Check if the customer has other addresses. If yes, the system may require designation of a new default before deletion (implementation-dependent).
     - If it's the only address and designated as default with pending orders requiring shipping address, reject the deletion (per section 562).

4. **Delete Address**: Execute a hard delete on the address record. Addresses are permanently deleted (not soft-deleted).

5. **Return**: Return 204 No Content on successful deletion.

**Database Operations**:
- SELECT address by addressId to verify ownership
- DELETE address record

**Error Cases**:
- 404 Not Found: Address doesn't exist or belongs to different customer
- 403 Forbidden: Customer not authenticated
- 409 Conflict: Cannot delete the only default address when pending orders exist (if implementing strict default address requirement)

Support pagination with limit/offset or cursor-based pagination. Sort by created_at descending (newest first) by default.

Include related user information (email, name) from parent tables for summary display. Exclude sensitive token values from response - only return metadata.

Return paginated result with session summaries containing: session id, actor type, user identifier, IP address, connection context, creation time, expiration time, and status.

operations.description:
Review and process a pending seller registration application.

Administrators use this endpoint to approve or reject seller registration requests. Upon approval, the seller can immediately begin listing products and selling on the platform. Upon rejection, the seller sees the provided reason and may submit a corrected registration.

When reviewing, the system records the reviewing administrator's identity and the review timestamp for audit purposes. Rejected registrations require a rejection reason which must clearly explain why the application did not meet platform standards.

After approval, sellers gain full access to product management, inventory, and order fulfillment features. The registration status becomes part of the seller's account history and is retained for platform governance purposes.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate administrator authentication and authorization.
Fetch the seller registration by registrationId.
Verify the registration status is 'pending' - reject if already approved or rejected.
Validate request body:
  - status: must be 'approved' or 'rejected'
  - rejection_reason: required if status is 'rejected', must be non-empty string
  - rejection_reason: must be null if status is 'approved'
Set reviewer_id to current administrator ID.
Set reviewed_at to current timestamp.
Set updated_at to current timestamp.
Update status field.
Update rejection_reason field (set to value if rejected, null if approved).
If approving:
  - Update associated seller account status to active/approved

operations.description:
Reset a user account password using a valid password reset token.

This operation allows customers, sellers, and administrators to complete the password reset process by providing their unique reset token and new password. The system validates the token against all three user type tables (customers, sellers, administrators), verifies the token has not expired, and updates the user's password hash.

Upon successful password reset, the token is permanently deleted to prevent reuse, and all existing sessions for that user are invalidated for security. The user must log in again with their new password.

The new password must meet platform security requirements including minimum length and complexity. If the token is invalid, expired, or the new password fails validation, the operation is rejected with an appropriate error.
operations.name: resetPassword
operations.specification:
Implement password reset using token validation:

1. Search for the provided token in all three password reset tables:
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_password_resets (token unique constraint)
   - ecommerce_mall_seller_password_resets (token unique constraint) 
   - ecommerce_mall_admin_password_resets (token unique constraint)

2. Verify the token exists and has not expired (compare expires_at/created_at with current time).

3. Retrieve the associated user from the corresponding actor table:
   - customers table for customer tokens
   - sellers table for seller tokens
   - admins table for admin tokens

4. Validate the new password meets platform security requirements (minimum length, complexity rules).

5. Hash the new password using the platform's password hashing algorithm.

6. Update the user's password hash in their respective table within a transaction.

7. Delete the used password reset token record to prevent replay attacks.

8. Invalidate all existing sessions for this user by deleting session records from:
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
   - ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions
   - ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions

9. Handle edge cases:
   - Return 404 error if token not found in any table
   - Return 410 error if token has expired
   - Return 422 error if new password fails validation
   - Use database transactions to ensure atomicity between password update and token deletion

requestBody.description: Password reset token and new password credentials

The response includes the token details including creation and expiration timestamps. If the token has expired, the client should reject the password reset attempt and prompt the user to request a new reset.

This operation supports all user actor types in the platform - customers, sellers, administrators, and super administrators - each having their own password reset record type.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of audit log entries from the platform's governance audit trail.

This operation provides comprehensive access to the audit logs that record all significant administrative actions performed on the platform. The audit trail captures who performed an action, what action was taken, which resource was affected, and contextual metadata including IP address, user agent, and timestamp.

The platform maintains two types of audit records:
1. Administrator audit logs - tracking seller approvals, category management, product oversight, order management, and user ban/unban actions by regular administrators
2. Super administrator audit logs - tracking critical security events including administrator promotions/demotions, system-level configuration changes, and force actions

This endpoint supports advanced filtering by administrator, action type, resource type, resource ID, date ranges, and IP address. Results are sorted chronologically with newest entries first, supporting cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large audit datasets.

Only administrators (admin and superAdmin roles) can access audit logs. Super administrators can view all audit records including those from other super administrators. Regular administrators have access to administrator audit logs but cannot access super administrator audit logs unless specifically authorized.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query both ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs and ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs tables based on the requester's privilege level.

For superAdmin requesters:
- Query both tables and aggregate results
- Include all fields: id, adminId/superAdminId, action/actionType, resourceType/targetType, resourceId/targetId, details/description, ip/ipAddress, userAgent, createdAt

For regular admin requesters:
- Query only ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs
- Restrict to records where admin_id matches requesting admin OR where resource involves accessible entities

Implementation logic:
1. Validate requester is authenticated as admin or superAdmin
2. Build WHERE conditions based on request body filters:
   - adminId: filter by specific administrator
   - actionTypes: array of action type strings (partial match supported)
   - resourceTypes: array of resource type strings
   - resourceId: exact resource ID match
   - dateFrom/dateTo: created_at timestamp range
   - ipAddress: exact or partial IP match
3. Apply sorting by created_at DESC (newest first)
4. Apply cursor-based pagination using created_at + id
5. Return paginated response with IEcommerceMallAuditLog.ISummary items

Edge cases:
- Empty result set when no logs match criteria
- Date range validation (dateFrom must be before dateTo)
- IP address format validation
- Action type case-insensitive matching

Error handling:
- Return 401/403 if requester lacks admin privileges
- Return 400 for invalid date formats or ranges
- Return 400 for malformed resource IDs

responseBody.description: Paginated list of audit log summaries matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering audit logs

operations.description:
Submit a request to become an administrator.

This operation allows registered customers and sellers to request elevation to administrator status. The request must include a reason explaining the user's qualifications, relevant experience, or motivation for seeking administrative privileges.

Upon successful submission, the request is created with 'pending' status and awaits review by a super administrator. Each user may only have one pending promotion request at any given time; attempting to submit a new request while one is already pending will result in a rejection.

The request is associated with the authenticated user (customer or seller) through polymorphic subtype relationships. Only users without current administrator status may submit promotion requests.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation requirements:

1. **Authentication**: Verify the user is authenticated as either a customer or seller.

2. **Authorization Check**: 
   - Verify the user does not already have administrator status
   - Query existing promotion requests for this user
   - Reject if any request with 'pending' status exists for this user (error: "You already have a pending promotion request")

3. **Request Validation**:
   - Validate reason field is provided and non-empty
   - Reason should have minimum length (e.g., 10 characters) and maximum length (e.g., 1000 characters)

4. **Database Transaction**:
   - Create record in ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests with:
     - id: generated UUID
     - status: 'pending'
     - reason: from request body
     - reviewer_id: null
     - rejection_reason: null
     - created_at: current timestamp
     - updated_at: current timestamp
   - Create corresponding subtype record based on user type:
     - If customer: insert into ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_customers
     - If seller: insert into ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_sellers
   - Both inserts must be in the same transaction

5. **Response**:
   - Return the created promotion request entity including:
     - id, status, reason, created_at, updated_at
     - Include requester information (customer or seller details)

6. **Error Handling**:
   - 401: User not authenticated
   - 403: User already has administrator status
   - 409: User already has a pending promotion request
   - 400: Missing or invalid reason field

7. **Side Effects**:
   - No snapshots created on initial submission (snapshots are created on status changes)
   - No notifications sent (administrators query pending requests)

responseBody.description: The newly created administrator promotion request with pending status

requestBody.description: Promotion request creation data including the reason for seeking administrator privileges

operations.description:
Approve or reject an administrator promotion request.

This operation allows super administrators to review pending promotion requests submitted by customers or sellers seeking administrative privileges. The super administrator can either approve the request, granting the requester regular administrator status, or reject the request with a reason.

When approved, the requester's status changes to approved and they gain administrator privileges. When rejected, the rejection_reason field captures the explanation for the denial, allowing the requester to understand why their request was not accepted and potentially submit a new request in the future.

The operation automatically sets the reviewer to the current authenticated super administrator and updates the review timestamp. A snapshot of the request state is created for audit trail purposes. Only requests with pending status can be reviewed; attempts to update already approved or rejected requests will fail.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting user is a super administrator. Verify the promotion request exists and has pending status - reject if already approved or rejected.

If status is being changed to 'approved':
- Validate no rejection_reason is provided (cannot reject and approve simultaneously)
- Set reviewer_id to current super admin's ID
- Create corresponding Administrator record for the requester with grade 'regular'
- Create AdminPromotionRequestSnapshot for audit trail

If status is being changed to 'rejected':
- Validate rejection_reason is provided and non-empty
- Set reviewer_id to current super admin's ID
- Create AdminPromotionRequestSnapshot for audit trail

Update the updated_at timestamp. Return the full promotion request entity including the reviewer relationship.

- The request is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp
- The requester (customer or seller) can submit a new promotion request if desired
- No notification is sent to the requester (silent removal)

Approved requests cannot be deleted as the user has already been promoted to administrator status. Rejected requests cannot be deleted as they serve as historical records of the decision with the rejection reason preserved.

Snapshots capture the complete state history of promotion request transitions. Each snapshot records the before and after states when a request's status changes (e.g., from pending to approved or rejected), including reviewer identities, status values, and associated reasons.

This operation provides audit trail visibility for:
- Super administrators reviewing promotion request history
- Compliance and security auditing
- Dispute resolution about promotion decisions

Snapshots are immutable records that preserve the exact state at each transition point. All fields including previous_review_id, new_reviewer_id, previous_status, new_status, previous_reason, and new_reason are captured for complete traceability.

- created_at date range
- previous_status / new_status
- previous_reviewer_id / new_reviewer_id
Join with ecommerce_mall_admins to get reviewer names for display (previousReviewer, newReviewer relations).
Return snapshot summaries including:
- id, created_at
- previous/new status transition
- previous/new reviewer info (id, name if denormalized)
- previous/new reasons
Exclude soft-deleted parent request snapshots only if parent is soft-deleted (though snapshots themselves are never deleted per immutability rules).
Return 404 if the promotion request does not exist or user lacks access.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product categories.

This operation provides browsing capabilities for the platform's category hierarchy. Categories support a maximum nesting depth of two levels: parent categories (top-level) and subcategories (one level below). Each category has a unique name within its parent scope and optional description.

The response includes category summaries optimized for list displays, showing essential information such as name, description, and parent relationship. Pagination follows standard page-based navigation with a default page size of 20 items.

Soft-deleted categories are automatically excluded from results. When a category is deleted by an administrator, it becomes unavailable for browsing but its history is preserved for existing orders and audit purposes.

When filtering by parentId, the operation returns subcategories belonging to that specific parent category. When parentId is omitted or null, the operation returns top-level parent categories.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table with pagination support.

Apply optional filters:
- parentId: Filter by parent category to get subcategories. When null or omitted, return top-level categories (where parent_id IS NULL).

Implement cursor-based pagination using createdAt and id as cursor fields for stable ordering.

Return paginated response with:
- data: Array of category summaries
- pagination: Cursor information for next/previous pages

Categories should be ordered by:
1. Parent categories first (null parent_id), then subcategories
2. Within same level, order by createdAt descending (newest first)

Include in summary:
- id, name, description
- parentId (null for top-level categories)
- createdAt, updatedAt
- subcategoryCount (if parent category, count of its subcategories)

Authorization: All authenticated users (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin) can access.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of category summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a single category by its unique identifier.

This operation returns complete category information including its name, description, and hierarchical relationships. If the category is a subcategory, its parent category details are included. If the category has subcategories, those are listed as well.

This endpoint supports the category browsing experience for customers navigating the product catalog hierarchy. Categories are organized in a two-level hierarchy: parent categories at the top level and subcategories nested beneath them.

Categories implement soft delete—deleted categories cannot be retrieved through this endpoint. If a category with no products is deleted, it becomes unavailable for browsing. Products in deleted categories become uncategorized but remain accessible through other means.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_categories table by id (UUID primary key).

Exclude categories where deleted_at is not null (soft deleted categories).

Join with parent category via parent_id relationship if parent_id is set.

Join with subcategories to retrieve child categories where their parent_id equals this category's id (excluding soft deleted subcategories).

Return 404 if category not found or has been soft deleted.

Include all scalar fields: id, name, description, parent_id, created_at, updated_at.

Include parent object with id, name if parent exists.

Include subcategories array with id, name for each active subcategory ordered by name ASC.

responseBody.description: Complete category details including hierarchical relationships

operations.description:
Create a new product category to organize products in the e-commerce platform.

This endpoint allows administrators to create categories that help customers discover products through hierarchical browsing. Categories support one level of nesting, meaning they can be either top-level categories (no parent) or subcategories of an existing parent category.

Each category requires a unique name within its parent scope. Name uniqueness comparisons are performed case-insensitively - names that differ only by case (e.g., 'Electronics' and 'electronics') are considered duplicates and will be rejected.

This operation is restricted to administrator users only. Customers and sellers cannot create categories.

When creating a subcategory (by providing parentId), the parent category must exist and not be deleted. The two-level hierarchy (parent + children) constraint prevents deeper nesting.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate the requesting user has administrator role. Validate the request body contains a non-empty name field and optional description and parentId fields.

If parentId is provided:
- Verify the parent category exists and is not deleted (deleted_at is null)
- The parent must be a top-level category (parent_id is null) to maintain the two-level hierarchy constraint

Check for duplicate category name using case-insensitive comparison within the same parent scope:
- If parentId is provided: check uniqueness within that parent_id
- If parentId is null (top-level): check uniqueness where parent_id is null
- If a category with the same name (case-insensitive) already exists in the same scope, reject with conflict error

Create a new category record in ecommerce_mall_categories table:
- Generate a new UUID for id
- Set parent_id from request (null for top-level)
- Set name as provided (preserve original case from input)
- Set description if provided, otherwise null
- Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
- Set deleted_at to null

Insert the record and return the complete category entity including generated id and timestamps.

Error scenarios:
- 401 Unauthorized: User is not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is not an administrator
- 400 Bad Request: Missing or invalid name, parent category does not exist, or parent is already a subcategory (would exceed 2-level depth)
- 409 Conflict: Category with the same name already exists within the same parent scope (case-insensitive)

responseBody.description: The newly created category with generated id, timestamps, and provided fields

requestBody.description: Category creation data including name, optional description, and optional parent category

operations.description:
Update an existing product category's information.

This operation allows administrators to modify category details including the name and description. Category names must be unique within the same parent category to prevent confusion in product organization. Top-level categories have globally unique names, while subcategories under different parents can share names.

Only administrators can update categories. Sellers and customers do not have permission to modify the category structure. This centralized management ensures a consistent and uniform taxonomy across the platform.

The category's hierarchical position (parent/child relationship) cannot be changed after creation through this operation. To reorganize categories, administrators must delete and recreate them with the desired structure.

Duplicate category names within the same parent scope are rejected with validation errors. The system performs case-insensitive uniqueness checks.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Validate the administrator's authorization to modify categories. Check that categoryId exists in ecommerce_mall_categories table.

Validate IUpdate request body fields:
- name: required, non-empty string, unique across all categories (case-insensitive check)
- description: optional string for category explanation

Perform unique name constraint check excluding the current category being updated. If another category already uses the requested name (case-insensitive), reject with validation error.

Update the category record with provided values. Preserve existing fields not included in the update.

Return the complete updated category entity including its id, name, description, parentId (if subcategory), and timestamps.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a category from the platform.

When a category is deleted, any products previously assigned to that category become uncategorized. Uncategorized products remain on the platform and can still be found through search and direct links, but they do not appear when customers browse by category.

If a parent category with subcategories is deleted, all its subcategories are also deleted. Products in those deleted subcategories become uncategorized as well.

Category deletion requires administrator privileges and cannot be performed by sellers or customers. Deleted categories cannot be recovered.

This operation performs a soft delete, preserving the category record for audit purposes while marking it as inactive.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the caller has administrator privileges.

2. Find the category by categoryId from the ecommerce_mall_categories table.

3. If category not found or already deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404 Not Found.

4. Check if the category has subcategories by querying ecommerce_mall_categories where parent_id = categoryId.

5. Begin a transaction:
   - Set deleted_at = current timestamp for the target category
   - For all subcategories (if any), set deleted_at = current timestamp
   - The database schema defines onDelete: Cascade for the parent relation, but we should explicitly handle subcategory deletion

6. Update all products in ecommerce_mall_products that reference this category or its subcategories to have category_id = null (uncategorized).

7. Commit the transaction.

8. Return 204 No Content with empty response body.

Edge cases:
- If category has active products, they become uncategorized (not deleted)
- Cascade deletion of subcategories happens automatically due to database constraints
- Soft delete preserves the category for historical reference in order snapshots

operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of products with optional filtering and sorting.

This endpoint allows customers to discover products through various search criteria including text search by product name, category filtering, price range filtering, and stock availability filtering. Results can be sorted by newest first, price ascending, or price descending.

The response includes product summaries optimized for browsing displays, containing the main thumbnail image, product name, pricing information, seller shop name, and average customer rating. Products without any variants are included in results but marked as unavailable for purchase.

Only active (non-deleted) products from approved sellers are returned in search results. The search uses GIN trigram indexing for efficient text matching on product names.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_products table filtering by deleted_at IS NULL to exclude soft-deleted products.

Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers to filter for approved sellers only (approval_status = 'approved' AND deleted_at IS NULL).

Apply search filters from request body:
- search: Use trigram similarity search on name field (GIN index) when provided
- categoryId: Filter by exact category_id match
- subcategoryId: Filter by category_id when subcategory is specified
- priceMin/priceMax: Filter by base_price range
- inStockOnly: When true, join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants and aggregate inventory from ecommerce_mall_inventory_records to filter products having at least one variant with quantity > 0

Apply sorting based on sortBy field:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC
- 'priceAsc': ORDER BY base_price ASC
- 'priceDesc': ORDER BY base_price DESC

For each product in results, calculate:
- priceRange: MIN/MAX of variant prices (or base_price if no variant override)
- averageRating: AVG of ratings from ecommerce_mall_reviews where deleted_at IS NULL
- reviewCount: COUNT of non-deleted reviews
- thumbnailImage: image_url from first image (display_order = 0) via ecommerce_mall_product_images
- sellerShopName: from related ecommerce_mall_sellers profile

Implement cursor-based pagination for consistent performance with large datasets.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product summaries with thumbnail, pricing, seller info, and ratings

requestBody.description: Product search criteria including text search, filters, sorting, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single product by its unique identifier.

 This operation returns the complete product information including the product name, description, category assignment, and base price. The response includes all associated product variants (SKUs) with their option values, individual prices, and current stock quantities.

 Product images are returned in their display order, with the first image serving as the main thumbnail. Seller information including the shop name and description is included to help customers identify the product source.

 Customer reviews and ratings for the product are also included, showing the average rating and individual review details. This comprehensive data enables the product detail page to display all necessary information for customer purchase decisions.

 This endpoint is accessible to all authenticated users. Customers can view any active product. Sellers can view their own products including hidden or suspended ones. Administrators can view all products regardless of status for oversight purposes.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_products table by the provided productId UUID parameter. Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variants to fetch all variants including their SKU codes, option values, prices, and calculated stock quantities from inventory records. Join with ecommerce_mall_product_images to retrieve all associated images ordered by display_order. Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers and ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles to get seller shop information. Join with ecommerce_mall_reviews and ecommerce_mall_customers to get review data including ratings and reviewer names. Join with ecommerce_mall_categories to get category name and hierarchy information.

 Implement authorization checks: allow customers to access active products only (products with at least one variant), allow sellers to access their own products regardless of status, allow administrators to access any product. Return 404 if product not found or user lacks permission. Calculate average rating from non-deleted reviews. Calculate stock quantity by summing all inventory records for each variant.

operations.description:
Create a new product listing on the platform.

This endpoint allows sellers to register new products for customer purchase. A product requires a name, description, category selection, and base price. The product is exclusively associated with the authenticated seller who creates it.

Only sellers with approved registration status can create products. Pending or rejected sellers are blocked from this operation until their registration is approved.

Upon successful creation, the product enters an active state. The product becomes visible in search results and category listings once it has at least one variant added. Every product edit (including creation) creates a snapshot preserving the product state.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the authenticated user is a seller with approved registration status. If status is pending or rejected, return 403 Forbidden.

2. Validate request body fields:
   - name: required, non-empty string, max length per business rules
   - description: required, non-empty string
   - categoryId: required, valid UUID referencing existing category
   - basePrice: required, positive number

3. Verify the category exists in the database. If not found, return 404 Not Found.

4. Create the product record with:
   - Generated UUID as primary key
   - name, description, basePrice from request
   - categoryId referencing the selected category
   - sellerId set to the authenticated seller's ID
   - createdAt timestamp set to current time

5. Return the created product entity with all fields populated.

operations.description:
Updates an existing product's details.

This operation allows sellers to modify their product information including name, description, category assignment, and base price. Only the product owner (the seller who created it) can perform updates.

Per the Snapshot Principle, every successful update automatically creates a product snapshot that preserves the previous state of the product and all its variants. This snapshot includes all product fields (name, description, category, base price, images) and variant states at that moment, enabling dispute resolution and audit trails.

The operation validates seller ownership before allowing any modifications. Attempts to update a product owned by another seller will be rejected. Soft-deleted products cannot be updated until restored.

Related operations: GET /products/{productId} to retrieve current state, POST /products to create new products.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement the following:

1. **Authentication & Authorization**: Verify the requesting user is an authenticated seller. Check that the product belongs to the requesting seller by comparing seller_id. Return 403 Forbidden if ownership mismatch.

2. **Existence Check**: Verify the product exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Return 404 Not Found if product doesn't exist or is deleted.

3. **Snapshot Creation**: Before applying updates, create a product snapshot record capturing the current state:
   - Copy all current product fields (name, description, category_id, base_price)
   - Create product snapshot image records for all current images
   - Create product variant snapshots for all variants of this product
   - Link the snapshot to the product for audit trail

4. **Field Updates**: Apply the provided fields from the request body:
   - name: Product display name (required in request)
   - description: Detailed product description (required in request)  
   - categoryId: Category assignment (required, must reference existing category)
   - basePrice: Base price value (required, must be positive number)

5. **Validation**: Validate all fields per business rules:
   - Name and description must be non-empty strings
   - Category must exist and not be soft-deleted
   - Base price must be a positive number

6. **Update Execution**: Update the product record in ecommerce_mall_products table, set updated_at to current timestamp.

7. **Response**: Return the full updated product entity including all fields (id, sellerId, categoryId, name, description, basePrice, createdAt, updatedAt).

Edge Cases:
- If seller registration is pending/rejected, block the operation (per Pre-Approval Operation Blocking rule)
- If category is changed, the product moves to the new category automatically
- Concurrent modifications: Use optimistic locking via updated_at timestamp to detect conflicts

responseBody.description: The updated product with all fields

operations.description:
Soft-deletes a product and removes it from active listings.

This operation allows sellers to delete their own products when they are no longer needed or available. The product is soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which removes it from search results and category listings while preserving the record for historical order reference and dispute resolution.

Before deletion, the system validates that there are no pending order items with 'paid' or 'shipped' status for any variant of the product, and no pending cancellation or refund requests.

Upon successful deletion:
- The product is soft-deleted and no longer appears in search results or category listings
- All product variants are cascade deleted
- All inventory records for those variants are removed
- All product images are removed from active listings
- Product snapshots are preserved for purchase history and dispute resolution

The operation returns the deleted product details for client state management.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Authorization: Verify the authenticated user is a seller who owns the product (seller_id matches authenticated seller).

2. Blocker Validation: Query order_items table joined with product_variants to check for any order items with status 'paid' OR 'shipped' belonging to any variant of the product. If any found, return 409 Conflict with error message indicating pending orders exist.

3. Service Request Validation: Query cancellation_requests and refund_requests tables joined with order_items and product_variants to check for any pending (unresponded) requests. If found, return 409 Conflict.

4. Soft Delete Execution: Set deleted_at timestamp to current time on ecommerce_mall_products record with productId. The schema defines onDelete: Cascade for related records, which will handle variants, images, and inventory records.

5. Return the deleted product entity including its soft-deleted state.

operations.description:
Reorder the images associated with a product.

This operation allows sellers to change the display sequence of product images, including which image appears first as the main thumbnail. Images are displayed to customers in the order defined by the seller.

When images are reordered, the new first image automatically becomes the main thumbnail that appears in search results and category listings. Sort orders must remain sequential without gaps, and each image must have a unique sort order within the product.

Image changes trigger product snapshot creation to preserve the visual state history for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Snapshots capture the complete set of images, their order, and which image was designated as the main thumbnail at that moment.

Only sellers who own the product can reorder its images. The system validates that the requesting seller has ownership rights before applying any changes.
operations.name: updateOrder
operations.specification:
Validate that the requesting seller owns the product identified by productId. Query all non-deleted images for the product from ecommerce_mall_product_images table ordered by display_order.

Validate the reorder request: ensure all image IDs in the request belong to this product, ensure no duplicate image IDs, ensure all existing images are included (unless specified otherwise by requirements).

Update display_order values for each image according to the new sequence provided in the request. The first position (lowest display_order) becomes the main thumbnail.

Create a product snapshot to record the image state change for audit trail. The snapshot preserves the complete set of images and their ordering at this moment.

Return the updated list of images with their new display_order values and image URLs.

Retrieve a specific product image by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete details of a single product image associated with a product. The image includes its URL, display order within the product's image collection, and creation timestamps.

The first image in the display order (order 0) serves as the main thumbnail for the product in search results and category listings.

Authentication is required to access product images. Sellers can view images for products they own. Administrators can view images for any product.

Validate both productId and productImageId are valid UUIDs.

- Include soft deleted images (they should still be retrievable)

Return 404 if image not found.
Return 403 if caller is a seller and does not own the product.

The image_url field contains a URI string referencing the stored image file.
The display_order field indicates the image's position in the product's gallery, with 0 being the main thumbnail.

created_at and updated_at timestamps use timestamptz format.

operations.description:
Upload a new image to a product.

Sellers can upload multiple images for each product they own. The uploaded image is associated with the specified product and becomes part of its visual presentation.

The first image uploaded for a product automatically becomes the main thumbnail image, which appears in search results and category listings. Subsequent images provide detailed views from different angles or show product features.

Images help customers evaluate products before making purchase decisions. High-quality visual presentation allows sellers to present their products professionally.

**Authorization**: Only the product owner (seller) can upload images. Cross-seller image management is blocked.

**Display Order**: The system automatically assigns the next available display order. The image at display order 0 serves as the main thumbnail.
operations.name: create

Validate that the authenticated user is the owner of the product (seller ownership check).

Determine the display order for the new image:
- Query existing images for the product where deleted_at is null
- If no images exist, assign display_order = 0 (becomes main thumbnail)
- If images exist, assign display_order = max(existing display_order) + 1

Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_product_images with:
- id: generate new UUID

- image_url: from request body
- display_order: calculated as above
- created_at: current timestamp
- updated_at: current timestamp
- deleted_at: null

Return the created image entity with all fields including the assigned display_order.

**Error Handling**:
- 404: Product not found or product is soft-deleted
- 403: Authenticated user is not the product owner
- 400: Invalid image URL format

operations.description:
Update a product image's display order to reorder images within a product.

This operation allows sellers to modify the sequence position of a specific product image. Changing the display order affects how images appear on the product detail page and determines which image serves as the main thumbnail (the image at display_order 1).

When an image's position is changed, the system automatically resequences other images to maintain gap-free ordering. All images within a product must have unique display orders starting from 1 without gaps.

Only the seller who owns the product can modify its images. Cross-seller image management is blocked per business rules. The operation updates the updated_at timestamp and returns the complete updated image record with its new display position.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
`Authenticate the requesting seller.

Validate product ownership:
- Load the product_image by productImageId from the URL path
- Join with parent product to verify product_id matches the path parameter
- Verify the product's seller_id matches the authenticated seller
- If ownership mismatch, return 403 Forbidden (cross-seller block)

Validate request body:
- display_order must be an integer >= 0
- display_order must be within valid range (0 to current image count - 1)

Execute reordering transaction:
- Begin database transaction
- If moving image to a lower position (earlier in sequence):
  - Increment display_order by 1 for all images with display_order >= new_position AND display_order < old_position
- If moving image to a higher position (later in sequence):
  - Decrement display_order by 1 for all images with display_order > old_position AND display_order <= new_position
- Update the target image's display_order to the new position
- Update the updated_at timestamp to now
- Commit transaction

Return the complete updated image entity including:
- id, product_id, image_url, display_order, created_at, updated_at

Edge cases to handle:
- Requesting same position (no-op, just update timestamp)
- Invalid display_order value (validation error)
- Image not found (404)
- Product not found or mismatch (404)
- Cross-seller access attempt (403)

If the deleted image was positioned as the main thumbnail (display_order 0), the next image in the sequence automatically becomes the new thumbnail.

The deletion uses soft delete semantics where the image record is preserved with a deletion timestamp for audit purposes and snapshot integrity. The image will no longer appear in the product's active image gallery or on product detail pages.

Authorization requires either ownership of the product (for sellers) or administrator privileges. Unauthorized deletion attempts will be rejected.

Reassign display_order values sequentially starting from 0 to eliminate any gaps caused by the deletion. Update each remaining image's display_order and updated_at timestamp. Return the deleted image record with its state at the time of deletion.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of product variants for a specific product.

Product variants represent specific purchasable configurations of a product, each identified by a unique SKU code within the product. Variants capture different option combinations such as color and size, allowing customers to select the exact configuration they want to purchase.

This operation supports filtering by stock availability status and searching by SKU code or option values. The response includes variant summaries optimized for list displays, showing SKU code, price (or base price if no variant override), and option values.

When retrieving variants for a product, only active (non-soft-deleted) variants are returned. Sellers can view all variants for their own products, while customers see only variants belonging to published products.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants table filtered by product_id from the path parameter.

Select fields: id, sku_code, price, created_at, updated_at, and related variant options.

Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options to include option_name/option_value pairs for each variant.

Support search filters in request body:
- Search by sku_code (partial match using GIN index)
- Search by option_name/option_value combinations
- Filter by in-stock status (requires joining with inventory records to calculate current stock)

This operation allows sellers to add SKU-level variants to their products. Each variant represents a distinct purchasable configuration defined by option combinations such as color and size. Every variant must have a unique SKU code within the product and can optionally specify a price override.

The variant becomes immediately available for inventory management and customer purchase once created. Option values (e.g., Color=Red, Size=Large) are specified in the request and stored in a normalized structure for efficient querying.

- Product not found or not owned by seller: Return 404 Not Found.
- Empty option array: Allowed (variant with no options).
